1. ABOUT JANATA COLLEGE

Janata College, established on 8thApril 1964, stands as a testament to the vision and dedication of a
galaxy of nationalists, philanthropists, and academicians who sought to spread the light of higher
education in this remote region of Barak Valley. Situated at Kabuganj, approximately 20 kilometres
south-east of Silchar in the Cachar district of Assam, the college has, for over six decades, served as
a beacon of learning and social transformation.

From its modest beginnings with a small number of pre-university students operating out of
Lakshmi Charan High School, Kabuganj (morning shift), Janata College has evolved into a premier
co-educational institution. It caters primarily to a rural population, including students from SC, ST
(Hills), ST (Plains), Tea Garden Labourer, OBC, and MOBC communities. As the only co-
educational institution of its kind in this part of the valley, the college takes pride in its inclusive
character and its significant contribution to women’s education, reflected in the notably high
enrolment of female students.

The college was initially affiliated with Gauhati University until 1993 and subsequently came
under the jurisdiction of Assam University, Silchar, in 1994. It was granted permanent affiliation
by Assam University during the academic session 2003–04. Over the years, the institution has
steadily strengthened its academic foundation and institutional framework. It was brought under
the Deficit System of Grants-in-Aid by the Government of Assam on 1st December 1975 and later
provincialized on 1st December 2005. The college is recognized by the University Grants
Commission (UGC) under Sections 2(f) and 12(B) of the UGC Act, 1956.
Janata College has undergone quality assessment by the National Assessment and Accreditation
Council (NAAC), securing accreditation in Cycle I (2004, Grade C+) and Cycle II (2023, Grade C).
Demonstrating its commitment to continuous improvement, the college has also submitted
institutional data for the NIRF 2024–25 and 2025-26 ranking. In alignment with global
sustainability goals, the college has declared its campus plastic-free under the motto “Beat the
Plastic Pollution” as part of its engagement with the APEX SDG initiative.

The year 2024 marked a significant milestone in the institution’s journey, as Janata College
celebrated its Diamond Jubilee, commemorating sixty years of dedicated service to higher
education in the rural landscape of Barak Valley.

Spread over approximately 7 acres of contiguous land, the college campus provides a conducive
environment for academic and co-curricular activities. The campus features a government-
constructed building enclosed by a pucca boundary wall, all-weather road connectivity, and a
serene natural setting enriched by ample greenery, including a well-maintained botanical garden.

With its enduring commitment to accessibility, inclusivity, and academic growth, Janata College
continues to play a pivotal role in shaping the educational and socio-cultural landscape of the
region.

2. VISION 2030, MISSION, Goals and objectives AND CORE VALUES

2.1 Vision Statement: Janata College Vision 2030
     To emerge as one of the premier institutions for inclusive higher education, transforming lives
     through innovative pedagogy, cultural preservation, and skill development, while maintaining our
     foundational commitment to serving marginalized communities and achieving recognition as a
     Centre of Excellence and autonomous status by 2030.

2.2 Mission Statement
     Provide accessible, quality higher education that integrates traditional values with
     contemporary competencies, develops skilled professionals from underserved region, fosters
     research in regional studies, and contributes to the sustainable socio-economic development
     of Barak Valley in particular and Northeast India in general through academic excellence,
     community engagement, and environmental stewardship.

2.3 Goals and Objectives
      To disseminate quality higher education among the rural and underprivileged sections of
       society, ensuring equity and access for all learners.
      To promote holistic development of students—intellectual, physical, emotional, & spiritual.
      To instil moral values, behavioural discipline, and a strong sense of social responsibility
       among students.
      To foster critical thinking, creativity, and scientific temper through innovative and learner-
       centric pedagogical practices.
      To implement flexible and outcome-based education in line with the National Education
       Policy 2020, including the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP).
      To encourage environmental consciousness and sustainable practices within and beyond
       the campus.
      To strengthen community engagement and partnership with all stakeholders.

3. FROM THE PRINCIPAL'S DESK

Dear Students, parents and all the stakeholders, it is my privilege &
pleasure to welcome you all to Janata College for the academic
session 2026–27. As a co-educational provincialized institution
under the Directorate of Higher Education, Government of Assam,
and affiliated to Assam University, our college stands committed
to upholding the highest ideals of education while remaining
deeply rooted in our regional ethos.
Education, as we believe, is a powerful instrument that dispels
ignorance and illuminates the mind towards righteous thought and
action. It empowers individuals, broadens their intellectual horizons, and enables them not only to
earn a livelihood but also to lead lives of dignity and honour. At Janata College, we cherish these
enduring values and strive to ensure that every student is equipped to live a life of self-respect and
purpose. We are equally committed to igniting the spark of creativity and curiosity in young
minds, nurturing them to become thoughtful and responsible citizens.

Established in 1964, Janata College has grown into a premier institution of higher learning in the
region. We take pride in our legacy of academic excellence and our continuous endeavour to foster
the holistic development of our students—encompassing body, mind, and spirit. Our mentor
system, under which students are grouped into six houses named after eminent icons of the North
East, ensures personalized guidance, emotional support, and a strong sense of belonging.

In alignment with the National Education Policy 2020, we have successfully implemented the
Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) from the academic session 2023–24. This
progressive framework offers multiple entry and exits options, along with a flexible and outcome-
based curriculum designed to meet the diverse aspirations of our learners. We have also submitted
our institutional data for the NIRF ranking and are diligently preparing for our upcoming cycle of
NAAC accreditation.

Our teachers are the pillars of this institution, and we continuously strive to equip them with
innovative and effective pedagogical strategies. Their dedication helps create a learning
environment that inspires academic curiosity, scientific temper, spiritual awareness, and emotional
resilience among students. At Janata College, we believe in maintaining a supportive atmosphere
governed by a framework of discipline that is firm yet flexible—one that encourages students to
learn, grow, and even learn from their mistakes.

To our dear parents, guardians, alumni, donors, and well-wishers, I extend my heartfelt gratitude
for your unwavering support and trust. Your partnership is invaluable in shaping the future of our
students. Together, we aspire to mould young minds into responsible global citizens of India who
can contribute meaningfully to society.

As the paradigms of education continue to evolve, let us collectively embrace change with vision
and determination. Let us take the arc of history into our hands and work together to build a
brighter, safer, and more innovative future. I warmly welcome all aspiring students seeking
admission into Higher Secondary (HS) and the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUG –
Arts). May your journey at Janata College be enriching, inspiring, and transformative.

With best wishes,
                                                                                          Dr. Debasish Paul
                                                                                              M.A. (Triple), Ph.D.
                                                                              Principal, Janata College, Kabuganj

6. BEST PRACTICES

Achievement of institutional excellence in any Higher Education Institute (HEI) lies at the core of
its best practices, which ensure quality and accountability. These practices set standards for
teaching, evaluation and governance, thereby building trust and transparency while promoting the
continuous improvement of the institution’s overall functioning. Beyond the conventional
domains of teaching, evaluation and governance, Janata College, Kabuganj remains committed to
sustainability, strategic engagement, social responsibility and capacity building through skill
enhancement. Some of the best practices of the college are:

     1. Structured Mentor–Mentee System: The College follows a well-organized mentor system
         wherein students are grouped into six houses named after eminent icons of North-East
         India. Each group is guided by dedicated faculty mentors who provide academic support,
         personal counselling, and continuous monitoring of student progress, ensuring a strong
         sense of belonging and individual attention.
     2. Inclusive and Equitable Education: True to its founding vision, the college prioritizes
         access to higher education for students from rural and marginalized communities,
         including SC, ST (Hills & Plains), Tea Garden Labourers, OBC, and MOBC groups.
     3. Holistic Development Approach
     4. Mashik Charcha: It is an initiative to share opinion or experience on some or any issue
     5. Student-Centric Teaching-Learning Practices
     6. Value-Based Education and Discipline
     7. Eco-Friendly and Sustainable Campus Initiatives
     8. Continuous Quality Enhancement Measures
     9. Faculty Development and Capacity Building
     10. Committed to fostering community engagement through Gramin Krira (rural sports) for
         women promoting sports, fitness and active lifestyles
     11. Community Engagement and Social Responsibility: The college maintains strong ties
         with the local community through outreach programmes, awareness campaigns, and social
         initiatives. This fosters a sense of civic responsibility among students while strengthening
         the institution’s role as a catalyst for regional development.
           These best practices collectively reflect Janata College’s commitment to quality education,
           inclusivity, and the holistic development of its students while remaining deeply connected
           to its community and environment

examinations are published within 7 days from the last examination.

A minimum of 75% class attendance is mandatory to appear in the Council/University
examination as a regular candidate. Student attendance is generally displayed on the notice board
before Puja vacation (September/October) for form fill-up.

21.2 Key Disciplinary Rules

      Students must always carry Photo-Identity Cards within the campus. Failure to produce
       them may debar students from attending classes.
      Use of mobile phones, cell phones, iPods, and MP3 players within the campus is strictly
       prohibited.
      Use of alcoholic beverages and hallucinatory drugs is strictly prohibited and will result in
       suspension or expulsion.
      Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited by the Supreme Court of India and will make a
       student liable for punitive/disciplinary action.
      The courses at Janata College are full-time; no student may simultaneously undertake
       another full-time course or job.
      Students must be in college uniform with the college emblem while within campus.
      Political or communal involvement affecting peace and harmony in the campus is
       prohibited.
      Parking place should be used for parking of two-wheelers, cycles, cars, etc.
      All powers of maintenance of discipline are vested with the Head of the Institution, whose
       decision shall be final.
      In case of emergency, a student can meet the Principal from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM. Group
       entry inside the Principal's chamber is strictly prohibited.

headquarters of Cachar. The college is accessible by all-weather road from Silchar via the Silchar-
